title: Fear In Gurbani
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 256
summary: Fear is carried here from  toward o Nanak, my doubts and fears have been dispelled, and the Messenger of Death.
whyItMatters: This shabad is useful when life feels afraid, guarded, dreading, because it keeps fear inside remembrance, conduct, and the Creator's larger care instead of private mood.
takeaway: Fear steadies when o Nanak, my doubts and fears have been dispelled, and the Messenger of Death.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਨੁ ਮਨੁ ਧਨੁ ਅਰਪਉ ਤਿਸੈ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਮਿਲਾਵੈ ਮੋਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: tan man dhan arapau tisai prabhoo milaavai moh ||
lines.translation: I offer my body, mind and wealth to anyone who can unite me with God.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਭ੍ਰਮ ਭਉ ਕਾਟੀਐ ਚੂਕੈ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਜੋਹ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: naanak bhram bhau kaaTeeaai chookai jam kee joh ||1||
lines.translation: O Nanak, my doubts and fears have been dispelled, and the Messenger of Death does not see me any longer. ||1||

structure: The opening movement names the pressure directly: .
The middle movement deepens the correction by holding the mind inside i offer my body, mind and wealth to anyone who can unite me with.
The closing movement leaves a return you can actually keep: o Nanak, my doubts and fears have been dispelled, and the Messenger of Death.
